_purpose: Estimates of what a model costs to serve, so that serving can be sized without a benchmark of your machine; `mcgyvr setup` does not read them. Every figure is an estimate for a card class. One card was read per class, so a class is a rough guide: speed depends on the card, not only on its memory. Most figures were taken through another server program (each reading's `backend` says which), with a file of the same model, usually of the same quantisation type; a reading's `note` says when it was not. None is a reading of your machine.

harness_caveats.summary: One server program's native generate API gave benchmark results far below those of the same weights served by llama-server, for some models.
harness_caveats.detail: Seen for the qwen2.5-coder 7b and 14b rows; yi-coder and deepseek-coder-v2 were scored correctly through the same path.
harness_caveats.consequence: No benchmark reading taken through that path is shipped.

harness_caveats.summary: One server program resolved qwen3-coder-30b-a3b's tag to a weight set of ~18 GB, not the Q2_K file this row describes.
harness_caveats.detail: On a card with less memory than that set needs, part of it spills to host memory, so a reading taken through the tag is of that set and its spill, not of this row's file. This row's Q2_K file was read under llama-server with some of its layers on the card (partial offload), and the row's memory figure is that resident part.
harness_caveats.consequence: Bind an explicit quantised file under llama-server.

harness_caveats.summary: The benchmark reading of gpt-oss-20b is disputed: it is attributed to an output budget too small in the harness.
harness_caveats.detail: First attributed to the MXFP4 quantisation; a later investigation attributed it to the harness's output token budget, not to the quantisation.
harness_caveats.consequence: No figure of that reading is shipped.

harness_caveats.summary: A model that fits a card's memory only marginally can run markedly slower rather than fail, so a marginal fit can look like a working one.
harness_caveats.detail: qwen2.5-coder:7b, read on a card with little memory left beside it, ran markedly slower than on a card of a larger class. The two cards differ in more than memory, so the cause is not isolated.
harness_caveats.consequence: A fit listing (`mcgyvr capabilities --vram`) keeps headroom for the KV cache above a model's memory figure, so a marginal fit is not listed as fitting.

backends._doc: What each server program offers and where it is limited.

limits: backend-native generate API is unsafe for benchmark measurement (CAV-01)
VRAM allocation is configured, not intrinsic — footprint is gpu-memory-utilization, not weight size
a card with little memory to spare beside the weights leaves it little room to batch in (CAV-04)

concurrency_findings.summary: Continuous batching scaled sublinearly, to 8.5x at 16 concurrent requests.
concurrency_findings.detail: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-AWQ under vLLM on one card of the finding's class: 1 req 68 tok/s, 2 req 127 (1.9x), 4 req 168 (2.6x), 8 req 289 (4.7x), 12 req 402 (6.6x), 16 req 489 (8.5x). Per-request latency stayed within 0.39-2.01 s throughout.
concurrency_findings.consequence: Per-source parallel capacity on a batching server can raise aggregate speed, with sublinear returns.

concurrency_findings.summary: Prefix caching returned a 43.3% hit rate on a shared 39-token prefix, and scales with prefix size.
concurrency_findings.detail: Over short coding tasks sharing one system prompt; 19% wall-clock speedup at that prefix length.
concurrency_findings.consequence: Directly relevant to the shared worker bundle: every local worker receives the same <=2 KB system prompt, which is roughly 50x the prefix measured here, so the benefit should be substantially larger in normal operation.

concurrency_findings.summary: A batching server can free nearly all the card memory it holds and return in about six seconds.
concurrency_findings.detail: Sleep 4.74 s, offloading the weights to host RAM and freeing nearly all the card memory the server held; wake 1.09 s. The endpoint stays up throughout; a container restart for the same effect took ~60 s. KV cache AND prefix cache are discarded on wake.
concurrency_findings.consequence: Can make two differently-sized rungs viable on one card. The discarded caches are the catch: a swap resets exactly the CON-05 benefit, so swapping mid-batch trades one optimization for another.

concurrency_findings.summary: Distinct models can run concurrently on one card.
concurrency_findings.detail: Three models (1.5B + 3B + 16B MoE), resident together on one card, completed in 23.6 s wall against ~44 s serial, each holding its solo throughput.

concurrency_findings.summary: Same-model concurrency scales 1.6–3.1x with server-side parallelism enabled.
concurrency_findings.detail: Requires the backend's parallel-slot setting; a single-slot server serializes same-model requests.

concurrency_findings.summary: Aggregate throughput across separate machines came close to the sum of each machine's own.
concurrency_findings.detail: Separate machines share no bus, so requests on one do not contend with requests on another for it.
